To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) institutional investors are unlikely to be motivated to engage with issuers in relation to the stewardship activities that the 2020 Code encourages; and (2) institutional investors should be encouraged to disclose their engagements in response to hedge funds and on systemic risks, and their engagements in response thereto.
the Stewardship Codes are not effective in fostering engagement with companies by institutional investors.
The 2012 Stewardship Code is a soft-law instrument which, as a matter of law and policy, is unlikely to be able to achieve its objective of increasing issuer-specific engagement by investors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of engagement under the Stewardship code.
whether the FRC’s stewardship code can be a meaningful tool for encouraging institutional investors to engage with issuers in a meaningful way.
the extent to which the 2020 update to the Code is likely to be effective and relevant in fostering issuer-specific engagement.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stewardship disclosure should be focused on the types of stewardship that are actually being undertaken by institutional investors.
the 2020 Code will not, in and of itself, lead to greater issuer-specific engagement by UK institutional investors.
, while there is a role for the Stewardship Regime, the Stewardship code is not the answer to enhancing the engagement of institutional investors with the companies in which it invests.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Stewardship Codes have been a success in the UK.
the 2020 Code has been a step in the right direction, but it is still a step short of the mark.
the Stewardship Codes have not been effective in promoting the engagement of institutional investors with issuers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stewardship engagement is unlikely to be significantly enhanced by the 2022 Stewardship Code, or by any future iteration of the Code.
the 2020 version of the Code is unlikely to be the Emperor’s New Code.

the 2020 Code should be seen as an opportunity to re-evaluate the nature of stewardship engagement under the UK’s Stewards Code, rather than as an opportunity to improve its impact on issuer engagement.
